newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close flat after BIL, Goodman results.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close flat after BIL, Goodman results.

text.p: * NZ shares end slightly down but off lows, moderate volume
* High turnover in Goodman Fielder, post-result
* Brierley down a cent after profit slightly below forecasts ---------------------------(Sept 5)---------------------------
381 nil * Volume NZ$57.5 million. Futures -2 at 1,125 698 nil * Other movers - +19 -7
Ord Minnett's Geoff Brown said locals may also have been selling on the realisation they were overweight in Goodman Fielder following a change in NZSE-40 weightings.

As a registered overseas company, GMF is now only included in the index to the extent it is owned in New Zealand, reducing its weighting to half a percent from 3.5. The annual result appeared in line with expectations, Brown said.

Brierley Investments' estimate of intrinsic worth at $1.40/share, up from $1.25 a year ago, was noted with interest as it announced an annual profit of $310 million, down from $432 million due to a sharply lower investment contribution.
Brown said the $1.40 was "probably a little bit understated" given the planned listing of BIL's major asset, U.K. Thistle Hotels, and the likely improvement in value next year for BIL.

Sky City, still basking in the afterglow of a strong result for its first five months of operation, touched $7.40 briefly but the main action was at $7.30, where one parcel of 250,000 shares changed hands.

Jim Patterson at First NZ Capital said that brokerage values the stock at $7, but there is variation between New Zealand and Australian valuations. He noted profit-taking in whiteware manufacturer Fisher and Paykel, down 13 cents to $4.87.
